GLOBALIZATION AND ECONOMIC STATECRAFT

Connections into leverage.

A short US–China AI chip case. Make a prediction, explore the evidence, then decide where you would investigate.

With Hao Xi · Prof. Hongying Wang’s course · About 5 minutes · Handout (PDF)

All content · Read at your own pace

YOUR FIRST THOUGHT

Can control become leverage?

A country controls technology its rival needs. Can it reliably stop the rival from obtaining it?

Choose a starting position, not a graded answer. You may change it or continue without choosing.

CASE BACKGROUND · 1 OF 3

A chip is a network of relationships.

Specialized AI computing relies on a globally fragmented supply chain: US firms design the chips, foundries abroad manufacture them, and specialized firms assemble and package the finished products. Commercial importance and sovereign authority are different questions: Washington does not own foreign factories, but uses legal jurisdiction over US-origin technology to control access.

Source: NVIDIA FY2023 annual-report bundle, PDF p. 98.

Reading lens · Chapter 2

Farrell and Newman connect network position with legal jurisdiction and institutional capacity. Which part would you need to examine here?

CASE BACKGROUND · 2 OF 3

A government restricts access.

In October 2022, the United States introduced controls on certain advanced computing chips and semiconductor-related activities. The rule cited national-security and foreign-policy concerns. It regulated covered items and transactions rather than establishing ownership of the supply chain. Assessing its effects requires tracing implementation as well as reading the rule.

Source: BIS, October 2022 rule, Summary, Federal Register p. 62186; part 734 amendments.

Historical case: these documents describe 2021–2026 episodes, not today’s export rules.

CASE BACKGROUND · 3 OF 3

Other actors have choices, too.

Global chip makers adapted by redesigning chips to fall just below technical control thresholds. Downstream developers optimized algorithms to train models on fewer chips. Chinese tech firms accelerated domestic chip development, while Beijing later restricted sales of modified chips that Washington had licensed. Consider the core puzzle: why would Beijing restrict imports of advanced chips that its own tech firms needed?

  • Adapt a productPreserve a way to serve customers.
  • Build domestic capacityInvestigate whether reliance on foreign inputs falls.
  • Use regulatory authorityInvestigate how another actor responds.
  • Hold back licensed importsAsk why Beijing would hold back chips its own firms needed.

Sources: NVIDIA FY2023, PDF p. 114; Chinese company report, p. 1; CAC notice, 31 July 2025; NVIDIA Form 10-Q, quarter ended 26 July 2026. Corporate accounts and regulatory allegations are attributed to their issuers.

Reading lens · Chapter 4

Goddard asks how international ties can give challengers influence. Domestic capacity and an international competing hub are different outcomes.

YOUR RESEARCH PRIORITY

Where would you start?

The US restricted AI chip sales to China in 2022. To judge whether this limits China’s access to advanced chips, where would you look first?

Choose a priority, not the only valid explanation. Be ready to give one reason.
